title: Object, block and file storage

kcs.statement: Block storage presents a raw volume to one server, which formats it with a file system. It gives low-latency random reads and writes for operating systems and databases; on AWS this is EBS and instance store.
File storage is a shared hierarchical file system that many servers mount at once over a network protocol such as NFS or SMB; on AWS this is EFS and FSx.
Object storage keeps each file as a whole object, with metadata and a unique key, in a flat namespace accessed over HTTP APIs. Objects are replaced, not edited in place; on AWS this is S3.

problem_ideas: Classify six needs as object, block or file: OS boot disk, shared home directories, 2 million product photos, a MySQL data volume, a team's SMB share, nightly log archives.
Explain why changing one byte in a 1 GB object means rewriting the whole object.
Twenty servers must read and write the same folder at once: which storage type?
A distractor offers block storage for serving images directly to browsers: why is it a poor fit?
Name the AWS services behind each type: block, file and object.
A database needs low-latency random writes: which type, and why not object storage?
